text:
ravi: heads-upwe had another eviction cascade yesterday on a shard where 4 tenants prefetched overlapping prefixes. idea: build a "credit controller" per-shard that gates prefetch admits and enforces proportional fairness.
jonathan: sounds promising. what's the admission signal? instant tokens or a leaky-bucket?
maya: lean toward credits that are earned by recent useful hits. credits = gamma*hits + delta*bytes_read to capture both hot small and large readers. credits decay over time.
sara: ops requirement: dedicated pools must not be starved by this controller. controller should support policy overrides per-pool (disable, baseline-reserve, strict).
ravi: implementation sketch:
- credits[T,S] maintained in shard runtime
- admit if credits[T,S] >= cost_estimate(P)
- cost_estimate = observed_prefetch_bytes * 1.2 bounded by config_max
- on demote/evict, tag reason and refund credits only for PREFETCH_CANCELLED or CLIENT_ABORT
- do NOT refund on HANDOFF/CLAIM or COMMIT evictions

jonathan: nit: make admit idempotent with request-token (retries from network won't double-charge). also need a cheap best-effort cost_estimate for wide prefixes.
maya: testing plan: synthetic mix of tenants: (hot-small qps, large-scan, bursty-poller). run on single shard with low evict threshold and compare eviction-count and hit-rate. add metric: "admit_credit_balance" per-tenant/shard.
sara: monitoring and safety: add kill-switch and per-node rollback feature flag. expose metric for refunds and refund-reasons so we can detect refunds masking handoff bugs.
ops-bot: created canary cluster: prefetch-credit-canary-01 in staging. will run default smoke for 3h and drop metrics at /staging/prefetch-credit/6781234567.
deploy-bot: canary deploy finished (2m 8s) :white_check_mark:
ravi: concern: race between handoff reclaim and refund path could allow a prefetched prefix to be re-admitted after a refund when it was actually handed off. invariant: refund only if eviction_reason in [PREFETCH_CANCELLED, OOM_PREEMPT] AND prefix_state == DEMOTED_NOT_HANDED_OFF. need a quick state check.
jonathan: agree. augment lease handshake to expose a cheap "was_handed_off_recently" bit or check epoch mismatch before refunding.
maya: also propose decay: credits = credits * exp(-dt/tau) so bursty tenants don't permanently hog. pick tau = 5m default.
sara: for dedicated pools, set baseline_credit = min(reserved_capacity_bytes, config_baseline). that ensures long-running tenants keep minimal prefetching.
ravi: I'll open a short RFC describing API (controller.Admit(token, tenant, cost), controller.Refund(token, tenant, reason), controller.Metrics()) and the desired invariants. tagging @jonathan @maya @sara for review. running canary tomorrow AM.
jonathan: add unit test for Admit idempotency and a fuzz test that injects random handoff/evict orderings to ensure we don't double-refund.
maya: +1. let's also surface "credit-debt" metric (bytes requested but throttled) so we can tune alpha/beta.
sara: sounds good. post-canaary gating: require no increase in handoff retries, <10% increase in overall evictions, and improved post-prefetch hit-rate for low-credit tenants.
ravi: thanks all. I'll paste RFC link here once written and set a review deadline of 24h.
